title: Filter Employees by Status Using IN
description:
Retrieve all employees whose employment status is either **'active'** or **'pending'**.

**Table: employees** — `id`, `name`, `status`, `department`

Return `id`, `name`, and `status`. Order by `name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, status VARCHAR, department VARCHAR); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Alice','active','Engineering'),(2,'Bob','inactive','Sales'),(3,'Carol','pending','HR'),(4,'Dave','active','Marketing'),(5,'Eve','suspended','Engineering'),(6,'Frank','pending','Sales'),(7,'Grace','active','HR'),(8,'Hank','inactive','Marketing'),(9,'Iris','active','Engineering');
solution_sql: SELECT id, name, status FROM employees WHERE status IN ('active', 'pending') ORDER BY name

test_cases.description: 6 employees are active (Alice, Dave, Grace, Iris) or pending (Carol, Frank)

hints: IN ('active', 'pending') is a concise way to write: status = 'active' OR status = 'pending'.
The IN list can contain as many values as needed, separated by commas.
explanation: WHERE status IN ('active', 'pending') matches rows where status equals any value in the list. Active employees: Alice, Dave, Grace, Iris (4 rows). Pending employees: Carol, Frank (2 rows). Total = 6. Bob, Hank (inactive) and Eve (suspended) are excluded.
